articles.headline: Bangalore traffic congestion rated world's worst for third consecutive year
articles.summary: TomTom's annual Traffic Index ranked Bangalore as the world's most congested city for the third year running, with average speeds below 15 km/h during peak hours. The BBMP and state government announced a comprehensive mobility plan including more dedicated bus corridors, while tech workers continue to demand hybrid work arrangements.

articles.headline: Karnataka Assembly election 2026: Congress vs BJP in high-stakes battle
articles.summary: The Karnataka Assembly elections scheduled for late 2026 are shaping up as a key political test. Congress's Siddaramaiah-led government faces corruption allegations while BJP's Basavaraj Bommai leads the opposition. Bangalore's 28 assembly seats — with their unique IT-wage electorate — are considered decisive battlegrounds.

articles.headline: NEET 2026 cancellation hits Bangalore's coaching industry; thousands of aspirants affected
articles.summary: Bangalore's coaching-industrial complex in areas like Rajajinagar and J.P. Nagar took a major hit after NEET-UG 2026 was cancelled following the paper leak. Over 2 lakh Karnataka aspirants were affected. Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation was welcomed by student groups but the retest date remains uncertain.

articles.headline: Bangalore tech layoffs continue as AI disruption reshapes the sector
articles.summary: Major tech companies in Bangalore's Silicon Valley of India announced fresh layoffs in 2026 totaling over 40,000 positions as AI-driven automation reshapes IT services. Entry-level coding jobs are being automated, forcing engineering graduates to seek reskilling in AI, data science, and product roles. The city's IT workforce participation is under strain.

articles.headline: Cauvery water dispute resolution brings relief; new desalination plant approved
articles.summary: The decades-long Cauvery water dispute took a step toward resolution with the Supreme Court mediating a new sharing formula between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. Meanwhile, Bangalore approved construction of a 500 MLD desalination plant on the coast to address chronic water shortages — particularly acute after the 2024-25 water crisis.

articles.headline: Metro Phase 2 completion transforms Bangalore's east-west connectivity
articles.summary: Bangalore Metro's Phase 2 lines — including the long-awaited east-west Purple Line extension — opened fully in early 2026, bringing the network to 100 km. Namma Metro now carries 8 lakh passengers daily, though public transport share remains below 30% of total trips.
